paragraph: In September 2025 the telecommunications ministry [put its 86-article draft Law on Artificial Intelligence on its public consultation portal](<https://consultapublica.minttics.gov.ao/storage/docs/Proposta%20de%20Lei%20Sobre%20a%20Intelig%C3%AAncia%20Artificial.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 6 May 2026, the Institute of Administrative Modernisation [held a public consultation session on the draft Digital Government Law](<https://ima.gov.ao/web/noticias/ima-promove-sessao-de-consulta-publica-sobre-o-anteprojecto-de-lei-do-governo-digital>). On 27 August 2026 [the portal showed 18 contributions from companies, 18 from specialists and 5 from the general public](<https://consultapublica.minttics.gov.ao/>). No report of the consultation, the comments received or a written answer to them has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

A [nationwide workshop on 18 April 2025 brought together public bodies, companies and civil society](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/burundi-validates-its-first-national-data-governance-strategy>) for Burundi's first National Data Governance Strategy. The strategy was [validated on 7 November 2025 at a workshop presided over by the Vice-Minister of Finance, Budget and Digital Economy](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/burundi-validates-its-first-national-data-governance-strategy>). In the last twelve months, the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Digital Economy [hosted the Central Africa Internet Governance Forum in Bujumbura from 16 to 21 February 2026](<https://finances.gov.bi/index.php/2026/02/19/le-burundi-accueille-pour-la-premiere-fois-le-forum-sur-la-gouvernance-de-linternet-en-afrique-centrale/>). It was a regional forum with no named national law or policy before it. No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

On 11 June 2024 a committee of the transitional legislative assembly [heard FED-numérique, Internet Society Burkina Faso and two independent specialists](<https://www.an.bf/storage/libelrapportcdd/eXnOdb937ARewNMzS8rzUcHTYyWJnXuZ5Nv4UF8i.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 17 June 2026, the Ministry of Digital Transition [held a national validation workshop](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article147201=>) on its draft national artificial intelligence roadmap for 2026 to 2030. There [government, the private sector, universities, civil society organisations and technical partners reviewed the draft](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/06/17/burkina-faso-validates-national-ai-roadmap-2026-2030-to-accelerate-digital-transformation/>). No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

A published notice [announces public consultations on the draft Cybersecurity Bill on 20 June 2025](<https://www.bocra.org.bw/sites/default/files/sites/default/files/documents/Preamble_to_the_Cybersecurity_Bill_Revised.pdf>). The consultations were open to all stakeholders, and the notice invites comments to the ministry by 23 June 2025. That is the one consultation on a digital law or policy held for Botswana in the past three years. In the last twelve months, a [National Data Strategy workshop](<https://dig.watch/updates/botswana-national-data-strategy-engagement>) was held from 7 to 11 September 2026, with no participant from outside government named. No report of what people said on the bill, and no written answer to them, has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

No stage is set. On 26 August 2026 the digital economy minister opened [a workshop in Bangui to validate the government's digital transformation strategies](<https://oubanguimedias.com/2026/08/28/la-centrafrique-se-dote-dune-feuille-de-route-strategique-pour-sa-transformation-numerique/>). Orange Centrafrique and its subsidiary Sofrecom carried out the studies behind them, under a World Bank-backed project. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, the statistics institute also held an [internal validation workshop](<https://www.icasees.org/index.php/actualites/328-icasees-atelier-de-validation-interne-du-projet-de-politique-de-diffusion-des-donnees>) of its data policy. No participant from outside government is named for either. No consultation of people outside government on a digital law or policy has been found. Preparing would need a named digital law or policy put to people outside government for their views.

In November 2024 [ARTCI opened a public consultation on a study of internet access pricing](<https://www.artci.ci/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Tarification_des_Services_dAcces_a_Internet_-_Novembre_2024_Reponse_OCI.pdf>). [Its website carries the written response Orange Cote d'Ivoire sent on 4 December 2024](<https://www.artci.ci/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Tarification_des_Services_dAcces_a_Internet_-_Novembre_2024_Reponse_OCI.pdf>). In the last twelve months, from 6 July to 6 August 2026, ARTCI [held a public consultation on net neutrality guidelines](<https://artci.ci/en/public-consultation-on-the-development-of-guidelines-for-the-implementation-of-net-neutrality-in-cote-divoire/>), open to all. On 13 and 14 August 2026 it [held a workshop at Assinie with telecom operators, internet providers and consumer associations](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2643946/economie/protection-des-consommateurs-lartci-harmonise-la-procedure-de-traitement-des-plaintes>). No source found says a rule required any of these consultations. Operating would need a consultation that a rule required.

The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications [put a draft decree on the personal data protection authority out for public consultation](<https://obs-cc.org/gouvernance-donnees-afrique-centrale-apdp/>) by September 2026, the observatory OBS-CC reports. In the last twelve months, the ministry ran that consultation under PATNUC, the government's digital acceleration project, and no date for its end is given. [In July 2025 a Yaoundé workshop on the universal digital service strategy included civil society and operators](<https://patnuc.cm/2025/07/11/numerique-pour-tous-le-cameroun-valide-sa-strategie-nationale-de-service-universel/>). No report of the consultation, no comments received and no written answer to them have been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

[In March 2025 the regulator ARPTC opened a public consultation on bringing 5G to the country](<https://actualite.cd/2025/03/18/larptc-lance-une-consultation-publique-sur-lintroduction-de-la-5g-en-rdc-communique>). In the last twelve months, on 6 August 2026, the digital economy minister [met people from the digital sector](<https://acp.cd/economie/rdc-larrete-interministeriel-sur-la-fixation-des-taux-ne-concerne-nullement-les-startups-reseau-des-acteurs-du-numerique/>) about an order of 20 July 2026 setting the sector's duties and fees. [A validation workshop on the draft national AI strategy, closed on 27 July 2026, included the private sector, academia and civil society](<https://www.mediacongo.net/article-actualite-166058_economie_numerique_les_participants_a_l_atelier_de_validation_technique_approuvent_le_projet_de_la_strategie_nationale_de_l_intelligence_artificielle.html>). In July 2026 the rights group ACEDH [said rural and indigenous communities had not been consulted on the RDC-PASS digital ID project](<https://acp.cd/economie/rdc-loperationnalisation-des-autorites-competentes-recommandee-pour-le-projet-rdc-pass/>). No report of a consultation, comments received or written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

On 8 and 9 June 2026 the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy [held a workshop in Brazzaville with 60 participants](<https://www.uneca.org/fr/stories/la-r%C3%A9publique-du-congo-veut-%C3%A9tablir-les-fondements-d%E2%80%99un-%C3%A9cosyst%C3%A8me-de-donn%C3%A9es-fiable>). The ministry held it with the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and GIZ. Its aim was to help draft the national data governance strategy. It followed a mission of 2 to 6 June that consulted 21 institutions, among them civil society and the private sector. That workshop is the consultation found in the last twelve months. No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

In August 2025 the information ministry [held a national validation workshop in Moroni on the new Code de l'information et de la communication](<https://www.al-fajrquotidien.com/reforme-du-code-de-linformation-aux-comores-entre-modernisation-necessaire-et-exclusion-contestee/>). [The national journalists' union, the SNJC, was in the room](<https://www.al-fajrquotidien.com/reforme-du-code-de-linformation-aux-comores-entre-modernisation-necessaire-et-exclusion-contestee/>). [Private, community and island media say they were not invited, and only the two state media attended](<https://www.al-fajrquotidien.com/reforme-du-code-de-linformation-aux-comores-entre-modernisation-necessaire-et-exclusion-contestee/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No report of the workshop, comments received or written answer to them has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

ARME, the country's regulator, [opened a public consultation on a proposed regulatory framework for satellite communication networks and services](<https://spaceinafrica.com/2026/08/05/cape-verde-opens-public-consultation-on-new-satellite-communications-regulatory-framework/>), which the trade press reported on 5 August 2026. In the last twelve months, submissions were open until 31 August 2026. The Conselho Consultivo da Economia Digital, a consultative council, [held its third ordinary meeting on 25 November 2025](<https://www.governo.cv/a-economia-digital-e-um-pilar-estrategico-para-o-crescimento-de-cabo-verde-ministro-olavo-correia/>), chaired by the minister. Nothing found states who answered the satellite consultation, or any view the council gave. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

Djibouti's Ministry of Digital Economy and Innovation [held a national consultation workshop on 22 January 2026](<https://www.unesco.org/fr/articles/djibouti-sengage-dans-lelaboration-dune-strategie-nationale-en-matiere-dia-alignee-aux-directives>) for the country's first national artificial intelligence strategy. About 80 participants came from ministries, universities, the private sector and civil society. In the last twelve months, that workshop is the consultation found, and [the contributions of business, civil society, young innovators and national experts are to feed the final text](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/djibouti-prepare-sa-strategie-nationale-d-intelligence-artificielle>). No report of a consultation on a digital law or policy, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

On 12 May 2025 High Commissioner for Digitalization Meriem Benmouloud unveiled the national digital transformation strategy. Le Chiffre d'Affaires reports it as [the result of broad consultation with ministries, experts, economic operators and digital actors](<https://lechiffredaffaires.dz/algerie-numerique-2030-une-strategie-ambitieuse-pour-un-virage-digital-inclusif-et-souverain/>). The report names no hearing, workshop or call for comment. No change has been found in the last twelve months. On 23 October 2025 the High Commission [launched a Scientific and Technical Committee of experts](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/algeria-appoints-expert-panel-to-accelerate-digital-overhaul>) to advise it, and no view it gave on a named law has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

MP Sahar Albazar wrote in September 2025 that the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology had [hosted a listening session for the private sector on the artificial intelligence bill](<https://oecd.ai/en/wonk/governing-ai-with-inclusion-an-egyptian-model-for-the-global-south>). More than 70 companies and experts attended and gave recommendations directly to officials. The National Telecom Regulatory Authority has its own [framework of rules and measures for public consultations](<https://www.tra.gov.eg/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Regulatory-Frame-on-the-Rules-and-Measures-of-Public-Consultations-003.pdf>), dated 2021, with no consultation under it named. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No report of the session or written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

The National Information Technology Agency [put its draft Data Harmonisation Bill 2025 out for public consultation](<https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/ghanas-data-harmonisation-bill-2025-to-be-opened-for-public-consultation-from-nov-19-to-27-2025.html>) from 19 to 27 November 2025. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the communications ministry [went clause by clause through the inputs on the misinformation and hate speech bill](<https://moc.gov.gh/2026/02/17/mocdti-engages-stakeholders-on-draft-misinformation-disinformation-hate-speech-and-publication-of-other-information-bill/>) at a two-day stakeholder meeting. The Cyber Security Authority [took comments on the Cybersecurity (Amendment) Bill from 1 October to 14 November 2025](<https://www.csa.gov.gh/public_document.php>). [Over 272 memos came in](<https://techfocus24.com/communication-ministry-seeks-private-sector-input-on-cybersecurity-act/>). No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

In April 2025 ANSSI, an agency under Guinea's Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy, [held a workshop to validate the draft State Information Systems Security Policy](<https://anssi.gov.gn/atelier-de-validation-de-la-politique-de-securite-des-systemes-dinformation-de-letat-pssie/>). Representatives of public institutions, cybersecurity experts and people working in the digital sector attended. In the last twelve months, the digital ministry and UNDP held [a validation workshop on a report assessing readiness for artificial intelligence](<https://guineematin.com/2025/12/20/intelligence-artificielle-guinee-rapport-national-feuille-de-route/>), reported in December 2025. No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

In July 2025 [the private sector, civil society and universities gave inputs on the draft National Data Policy](<https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/gambia/gambia-moves-closer-stronger-data-governance-validating-its-national-data-policy-validated_en>) at a validation workshop. In the last twelve months, on 2 April 2026, the regulator PURA [published the draft Broadcasting and Online Content Regulations, 2026](<https://pura.gm/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Broadcasting-and-Online-Content-Regulations-2026-.pdf>) with six other draft instruments. It [invited licensees, industry, civil society and the general public to comment](<https://pura.gm/public-consultation-guidelines-and-notice/>) between 1 and 10 April 2026. No consultation report from the last three years has been found, nor the comments received or a written answer to them. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

On 17 July 2026 ARN [published its report on a consultation on the draft radio spectrum fees order](<https://arn.gw/activeapp/noticias/arn-publica-relatorio-da-consulta-publica-n-o-2-sobre-o-projeto-de-despacho-das-taxas-radioeletricas/>). [It set out Orange Bissau's contribution, the only one, and which proposals it accepted or refused](<https://arn.gw/activeapp/noticias/arn-publica-relatorio-da-consulta-publica-n-o-2-sobre-o-projeto-de-despacho-das-taxas-radioeletricas/>). Before that, on 30 October 2025, a workshop [presented the draft universal access and service law, decree and policy to stakeholders](<https://wardip.gw/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Documento-Final-de-Validacao-do-Workshop.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 8 May 2026, the regulator ARN-TIC [opened a public consultation on the draft Electronic Transactions Law](<https://www.odemocratagb.com/?p=57171>). The spectrum fees report cites a law but does not say it required the consultation. Operating would need a consultation that a rule required.

On 26 August 2025 the ICT ministry and the Communications Authority [asked the public for views](<https://ict.go.ke/kica-regulations-documents-2026>) on the draft Kenya Information and Communications Regulations. The ministry later [published a matrix of the comments beside the revised drafts](<https://ict.go.ke/kica-regulations-documents-2026>). In the last twelve months, on 22 September 2026, the Authority [published the submissions on its internet telephony guidelines with its own position](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/09/22/kenya-ca-finalise-commercial-internet-telephony-guidelines/>). The draft AI policy [was open for written comment from 21 July to 4 August 2026](<https://ict.go.ke/sites/default/files/AI%20Policy%20Doc/draft-kenya-ai-and-emerging-technologies-policy-2026.pdf>). No standing body with members from outside government has been found giving its view on a named digital law or policy. Mature would need a standing body with members from outside government to give its view on a named digital law or policy.

The Liberia Telecommunications Authority [put its draft Satellite Communications Guidelines out for comment](<https://lta.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/CONSULTATION-DOCUMENT-SATELLITE-COMMUNICATIONS-GUIDELINES-FINAL-COPY.pdf>) from 23 February to 9 March 2026. On 3 April 2026 it [published a Consultation Report](<https://www.liberianobserver.com/news/lta-signs-new-satellite-framework-targets-digital-access-across-liberia/article_e178022e-dcdf-47e5-a31b-9abefbb594c2.html>) answering the written submissions. Its document says it [followed the Authority's Guidelines for Consultation Process of 2009](<https://lta.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/CONSULTATION-DOCUMENT-SATELLITE-COMMUNICATIONS-GUIDELINES-FINAL-COPY.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 9 October 2026, the Authority [held a public consultation on draft Infrastructure Regulations](<https://www.liberianobserver.com/news/lta-holds-public-consultation-on-draft-infrastructure-regulations/article_f187f32e-dd53-4c5e-8645-7e26476124be.html>) in Paynesville. No source reports a standing body with outside members giving its view. Mature would need a standing body with members from outside government to give its view on a named digital law or policy.

The ICT ministry [circulated the draft Cybersecurity Bill 2026 for stakeholder review](<https://www.gov.ls/development/stakeholders-engage-on-cybersecurity-bill-2026/>) in August 2026. In the last twelve months, on 23 September 2026, it opened a second two-day workshop on the bill in Maseru, with the Lesotho Communications Authority and UNDP. The ministry also [launched a National Cybersecurity Forum in July 2026](<https://www.gov.ls/development/stakeholders-engage-on-cybersecurity-bill-2026/>) with public bodies, companies, academics, civil society and the technical community. It [first met in Maseru on 29 July 2026](<https://www.gov.ls/ict/ministry-of-information-communications-science-technology-and-innovation-launched-lescomcsirt-and-inaugural-national-cybersecurity-forum/>). No consultation report, comments received or written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

On 7 September 2026 the minister delegate for digital transition, Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni, [held a dialogue in Rabat](<https://lenew.ma/inclusion-numerique-le-gouvernement-mise-sur-les-jeunes-les-femmes-et-les-personnes-en-situation-de-handicap/>). [More than 100 participants came from civil society, administrations, institutions and universities](<https://lenew.ma/inclusion-numerique-le-gouvernement-mise-sur-les-jeunes-les-femmes-et-les-personnes-en-situation-de-handicap/>). Their proposals [are to feed the update of the third national Open Government action plan, for 2024 to 2028](<https://lenew.ma/inclusion-numerique-le-gouvernement-mise-sur-les-jeunes-les-femmes-et-les-personnes-en-situation-de-handicap/>). In the last twelve months, that dialogue is the consultation found, and it concerned the plan's digital inclusion commitments. No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

On 11 September 2024 the telecoms regulator ARTEC [held a public consultation workshop on a draft decree on spectrum and numbering](<https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7239950779405524992>). [Operators, frequency users, civil society and ministries took part](<https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7239950779405524992>). [ARTEC says the workshop was held to finalise the text](<https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7239950779405524992>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No report of the workshop, comments received or written answer to them has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

From 4 May to 4 June 2026 the National Institute of Information and Communication Technologies (INTIC) [invited comments on the first version of the draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy](<https://intic.gov.mz/consulta-publica-da-proposta-da-estrategia-nacional-de-inteligencia-artificial/>). Public and private institutions, academia, development partners and citizens could reply by email. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the ministry [launched a public consultation on the national digital transformation strategy](<https://www.oeconomico.com/governo-mobiliza-o-pais-para-definir-estrategia-nacional-de-transformacao-digital-e-aposta-na-interoperabilidade-como-eixo-estruturante/>). A [validation workshop in Nampula on 18 May 2026 closed the provincial consultations](<https://intic.gov.mz/consultas-publicas-sobre-transformacao-digital-entram-em-fase-de-validacao-em-nampula/>). No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

The Ministry of Digital Transformation, Innovation and Administrative Modernisation [held a validation workshop in Nouakchott on the draft national e-commerce strategy for 2026 to 2030](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/281808>), which the news agency AMI reported on 28 October 2025. [Among them were representatives of companies, civil society and academia](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/281808>). In the last twelve months, on 7 May 2026, the WARDIP-Mauritanie project [published a provisional award notice for technical assistance to build a national platform for citizen participation](<https://mtnima.gov.mr/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Attribution-provisoire_platforme-citoyenne.pdf>). The notice is a procurement and names no digital law or policy put to the public. No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

On 23 August 2024 the Information and Communication Technologies Authority [issued a consultation paper](<https://www.icta.mu/public-consultations/>) on more spectrum for mobile services. [Its response to the paper, dated 7 November 2024](<https://www.icta.mu/public-consultations/>), sits beside it on the Authority's public consultations register. On 15 April 2025 the ICT ministry [put its draft child online safety report out for comment until 30 April](<https://mitci.govmu.org/mitci/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Public-Consultation-on-Child-Online-Safety-Draft-Report.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source from the last three years says a consultation was held because a rule required it. Operating would need a consultation that a rule required.

MACRA, acting as the Data Protection Authority, [held a consultation meeting in Lilongwe on 15 July 2026](<https://www.nyasatimes.com/macra-consults-stakeholders-on-proposed-data-protection-registration-fees/>) on draft data protection regulations and registration fees. A later [validation workshop on the fees in Blantyre](<https://www.dpa.mw/dpa-reviews-proposed-data-protection-registration-fees/>) brought in public and private sector representatives. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the Department of E-Government [opened a two-day validation workshop in Lilongwe](<https://leymanck.com/ministry-validates-digital-transformation-and-ai-strategies/>) on the draft National Digital Transformation Strategy and the draft National AI Strategy. Regulators, companies, civil society and academia took part. No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

In February 2026 the ICT ministry [held a public stakeholders' engagement in Windhoek](<https://www.thevillager.com.na/national/2026/cybercrime-bill-in-the-pipeline-for-namibia/>) on the draft Cybercrime Bill. It [took the bill to Rundu, where police and residents took part, and invited written submissions until 10 February 2026](<https://www.nbcnews.na/node/114959>). In the last twelve months, in April 2026, it [held a validation workshop on the final draft](<https://www.namibian.com.na/problems-with-the-cybercrime-bill/>), though many civil society groups say they had little or no notice. In November 2026 CRAN [held a stakeholder consultation](<https://thebrief.com.na/2026/11/cran-develops-regulatory-framework-for-ai-satellite-internet-and-blockchain/>) on a proposed regulatory sandbox for AI, satellite broadband and other new technologies. No consultation report, comments received or written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

On 20 July 2026 ARCEP, the telecoms regulator, [launched a public consultation](<https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/telecom-regulation/20557-niger-kicks-off-public-consultation-on-5g-spectrum-plan.html>) on reorganising the spectrum plan for 5G. [It ran to the end of August 2026](<https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/telecom-regulation/20557-niger-kicks-off-public-consultation-on-5g-spectrum-plan.html>) and was open to anyone. In the last twelve months, on 18 and 19 May 2026, the national communication observatory also [held a workshop in Maradi on the draft ordinance on the electronic press](<https://anp.ne/maradi-cloture-de-latelier-sur-la-presse-electronique-avec-adoption-de-plusieurs-recommandations/>). [Journalists, online media owners, web activists and influencers reviewed and amended the draft](<https://anp.ne/maradi-cloture-de-latelier-sur-la-presse-electronique-avec-adoption-de-plusieurs-recommandations/>). No report of a consultation, comments received or written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

On 10 November 2025 the National Assembly [held a hearing on the Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill](<https://techcabal.com/2025/11/11/nigerias-digital-economy-bill-hands-sweeping-powers-to-nitda/>). The Communications Commission held public inquiries on 11 and 12 November 2025 on its draft Internet Code of Practice [under section 57 of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003](<https://www.ncc.gov.ng/media-center/public-notices/public-inquiries-draft-internet-code-practice-and-draft-regulations>). In the last twelve months, on 23 July 2026, the Senate [held a public hearing on bill SB648, which amends the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023](<https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/07/project-sprint-rallies-senate-support-for-data-protection-bill/>). On 19 June 2026 the Commission [issued a consultation paper on zero-rated access to educational platforms](<https://www.ncc.gov.ng/sites/default/files/2026-06/Consultation-Paper-on-Zero-Rated-Access-to-Educational-Platforms.pdf>). No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

On 12 February 2026 the Capital Market Authority [put its draft regulation on intermediary service platform operators out for comment](<https://www.cma.rw/news-publications/press-center/call-for-public-comments-on-the-draft-regulation-governing-intermediary-service-platform-operators>). The regulation covers fintech firms. The Authority asked fintech experts, lawyers, bankers, payment firms and investors for their views, and said a consultation meeting would follow. In the last twelve months, that call is the consultation found. In June 2025 the Data Protection and Privacy Office [began workshops with health, media and education stakeholders on sector data protection guides](<https://dpo.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/Newsletter_June_2025.pdf>). No report of a consultation, comments received or written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

Skyline International for Human Rights says [the Cabinet approved amendments to the Cybercrime Law on 13 October 2025 without transparency or public consultation](<https://skylineforhuman.org/en/news/details/875/sudans-draconian-cybercrime-law-amendments-pose-grave-threat-to-digital-freedoms>). It asks for a [review of such laws in consultation with civil society, journalists' unions and legal experts](<https://skylineforhuman.org/en/news/details/875/sudans-draconian-cybercrime-law-amendments-pose-grave-threat-to-digital-freedoms>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source from the last three years says people outside government were asked for their views on a digital law or policy. Preparing would need a named digital law or policy put to people outside government.

In March 2026 the telecoms regulator ARTP [launched a public consultation on deploying and sharing fibre networks to the subscriber](<https://artp.sn/partage-infrastructures/fttx>). On 10 August 2026 it [published a synthesis of the twenty-one contributions](<https://artp.sn/partage-infrastructures/fttx>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026, ARTP also [asked sector actors for their views on licensing and obligations for satellite operators](<https://www.osiris.sn/satellite-et-reseaux-terrestres-le-senegal-ajuste-son-cadre-reglementaire.html>), until 21 October. The [Conseil national du Numérique is a consultative body of 20 public, private and civil-society members](<https://primature.sn/publications/actualites/installation-officielle-du-conseil-national-du-numerique-cnn-du-senegal>). No source found says a rule required a consultation, or that the Conseil gave its view on a named law. Operating would need a consultation that a rule required.

In November 2025 the information minister said the [Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill, 2025 had finished its final national validation](<https://sierraloaded.sl/news/government-data-protection-information-bill>). Civil society, media, academia and the private sector gave drafting input alongside Parliament and state bodies. In the last twelve months, Cabinet [approved the National Data Protection Policy and a new data protection and access to information law](<https://moice.gov.sl/cabinet-approves-first-ever-data-protection-policy-paving-way-for-new-data-law/>), reported on 22 April 2026. The ministry MoCTI [held the first meeting of its Technology, Innovation and Entrepreneurship Advisory Council](<https://mocti.gov.sl/mocti-holds-its-inaugural-meeting-of-the-technology-innovation-and-entrepreneurship-advisory-council-tieac/>), reported on 5 February 2026. No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

The National Communications Authority [held a one-day consultation on 16 February 2026](<https://nca.gov.so/nca-holds-consultation-on-telecom-consumer-protection-regulation/>) on its draft Telecom Consumer Protection Regulation. Operators, internet providers, submarine cable operators and consumer representatives gave their views. In the last twelve months, the Authority also [convened a national consultation meeting](<https://nca.gov.so/national-communications-authority-holds-consultation-meeting-on-cybersecurity-risk-management-and-compliance-framework/>), reported on 25 April 2026, on its draft Cybersecurity Risk Management and Compliance Framework. Government institutions, private companies, the education sector, civil society and technical experts took part. No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

The National Communication Authority and Digital Rights Frontlines, a civil society group, [convened a two-day workshop on the Data Protection Bill 2025](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/digital-rights-frontlines_dataprotection-digitalrights-cybersecurity-activity-7457423027161620480-l2o_>), reported on 5 May 2026. More than 30 people took part, among them members of parliament and civil society groups. In the last twelve months, a [ministry workshop in Juba on 8 to 10 September 2026](<https://www.kictanet.or.ke/south-sudan-data-governance-workshop-juba/>) prepared for the same bill, with about 50 people including civil society groups and telecom operators. In October 2025 the chair of the Assembly's Information Committee said its work on the cybercrime bill [included public consultations and workshops](<https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/south-sudan-lawmakers-advance-cybercrime-bill-to-final-vote>). No published report, comments received or written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

In September 2025 AGER, under the STP Digital project, [put the National Cybersecurity Strategy of São Tomé and Príncipe 2024-2028 out for public consultation](<https://www.ager.st/index.php/pt/actualidades/19-annonces/106-estrategia-nacional-de-ciberseguranca-de-sao-tome-e-principe>), together with the action plan annexed to it. It invited contributions by telephone and by email within 30 days of publication. In the last twelve months, AGER [convened the first Fórum de Governança da Internet de São Tomé e Príncipe on 28 to 30 July 2026](<https://www.ager.st/index.php/en/news/19-annonces/122-ager-realiza-com-sucesso-a-1-edicao-do-fgi-stp>). It was not a consultation on a named law or policy. No published report of a consultation, the comments received or a written answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

The Eswatini Communications Commission, ESCCOM, opened a consultation on retiring 2G and 3G networks on 9 November 2024. Its [final decision of 17 June 2025](<https://esccom.org.sz/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Notice-5-Notice-on-Legacy-Networks.pdf>) summarises the comments stakeholders sent and sets out its response to them. In the last twelve months, the Ministry of ICT held [a two-day validation session in February 2026](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ministry-of-ict-eswatini_rsti-stipolicyreview-digitaltransformation-activity-7432119915588812800-2Nv->) on the draft National STI Policy review and the 4IR and 5IR Strategy. None names a law, decree or published procedure that required a consultation. Operating would need a consultation that a rule required.

On 20 December 2023 the Financial Services Authority, for the Ministry of Finance, [launched a public consultation on the proposed Virtual Asset Service Providers framework](<https://www.finance.gov.sc/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Virtual-Asset-Service-Providers-Framework-Response-to-Public-Consultation.pdf>). The Ministry and the Authority [published a consultation response dated 7 March 2024](<https://www.finance.gov.sc/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Virtual-Asset-Service-Providers-Framework-Response-to-Public-Consultation.pdf>), which summarises about 15 detailed written responses. In the last twelve months, a member of the drafting team says the [National Digital and AI Strategy 2026-2031 followed consultations with the private sector, academia and civil society](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/baidy-s-91972228_digitaltransformation-ai-digitalgovernment-activity-7481275398413152257-B36W>). No source found says a rule required a consultation on a digital law or policy. Operating would need a consultation that a rule required.

Its head of legal affairs said the hearing [was required by article 43 of the audiovisual communication law](<https://lendjampost.com/media-le-projet-portant-cahier-de-charge-des-web-radios-et-televisions-presente-par-la-hama/>). In the last twelve months, the telecommunications ministry, with ECA and GIZ, [held consultations in N'Djamena on 13 to 15 May 2026](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/eca-supporting-chad-developing-national-data-governance-strategy-advance-au-data-policy-framework>) for the National Data Governance Strategy. On 7 October 2026 it [held a national validation workshop on the draft strategy](<https://mten.gouv.td/discours-de-haliki-choua-mahamat-sur-la-gouvernance-des-donnees/>). No published report of a consultation, the comments received or the government's answer has been found. Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

Regulatory authorities, academic institutions and sectoral agencies gave their views. In the last twelve months, on 20 October 2026, Parliament's Standing Committee on Infrastructure [invited the public to give views on ratifying the Malabo Convention](<https://dailynews.co.tz/bunge-committee-invites-views-on-data-protection/>). Establishing would need a published report, the comments or the written answer.

In the last twelve months, on 20 October 2026, the communications regulator, UCC, [met the Kampala City Traders Association and Wi-Fi hotspot operators](<https://publicisteastafrica.com/can-uganda-build-a-legal-public-wi-fi-revolution/>). It announced a multi-stakeholder committee on licensing for resellers, which has not yet given a view. [It invited operators, importers, civil society, academics and the public to comment until 20 November 2026](<https://ib-lenhardt.com/media/pages/news/consultation-on-draft-revised-type-approval-guidelines/3220b471e8-1792662126/public-notice-draft-revised-type-approval-guidelines_20102026.pdf>).
